# cpanel_email_filter (Data Source)

Looks up one user-level cPanel email filter for an existing mailbox, including its ordered rules, ordered actions, and enabled state. The data source can observe external `save` and `pipe` actions even though the resource deliberately does not manage them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "cpanel_email_filter" "important" {
  account = "inbox@example.com"
  name    = "Important messages"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account` (String) The mailbox that owns the user-level filter.
- `name` (String) The cPanel filter name.

### Read-Only

- `actions` (Attributes List) The ordered actions performed when the rules match. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether cPanel evaluates the filter.
- `rules` (Attributes List) The ordered conditions evaluated by cPanel. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions`

Read-Only:

- `action` (String) The action type.
- `destination` (String) The action destination, when applicable.


<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Read-Only:

- `match` (String) The comparison applied by the rule.
- `operator` (String) The connection to the next rule, or `none` for the final rule.
- `part` (String) The email section inspected by the rule.
- `value` (String) The value matched by the rule.
